shrub.silhouette: low dark evergreen mound, pink flowers

growth.juvenile_note: Minute seedlings on moss or raw humus: two tiny cotyledons, then small glossy, dark green, leathery leaves with rusty-brown scaly undersides and rolled edges. For years it is a small, few-stemmed sprig; then it branches densely into a low, rounded evergreen bush, and stems that touch the ground root and spread it into a clonal patch.
growth.source: German Wikipedia Rostblaettrige Alpenrose (30-130 cm; stems 1-2 cm thick nearly 100 yr old; leaves live ~2 yr; flowers May-Jul, corolla to 2 cm, deep pink to red; capsules to 7 mm ripen from August; semi-shade light value; 440-2,840 m); germination and first flowering estimated

fruiting.source: German Wikipedia (flowers May-Jul in terminal clusters, funnel-bell corolla to 2 cm, deep pink to red; capsules to 7 mm ripening from August); bumblebee pollination and poisonous grayanotoxins from knowledge; truss size, set and crop estimated

shrub.silhouette: dark sprawling pine mound, knee to head high

growth.juvenile_note: Seedlings have 5-7 cotyledons and a tuft of short primary needles; the young plant soon branches from the base into a low, dense, rounded bush of stiff, dark-green, paired, curved needles. Stems lie downhill under snow and rise at the tips, so old plants form thickets of crooked, interlaced, ground-hugging branches.
growth.source: Wikipedia (subsp. mugo a low, shrubby, often multi-stemmed plant to 3-6 m; cones 2.5-5.5 cm, nut-brown); growth, first cones and lifespan estimated from treeline dwarf-pine studies in the Alps

fruiting.source: Wikipedia (cones 2.5-5.5 cm, nut-brown, matt and symmetrical in subsp. mugo); two-season pine cone cycle, violet young cones and empty cones lingering on the branches estimated from the genus

traits.native_range: Castilleja rhexiifolia, Rocky Mountain subalpine/alpine meadows 2500-3800 m, magenta bracts 10-40 cm
traits.note: leaf/trunk/petiole derived from the plant's shape class; per-species detail where the entry carries it (aroids, cannabis)

growth.juvenile_note: Tiny oval cotyledons, then a short upright stem of narrow lance-shaped leaves; it tastes host roots (grasses, forbs) with haustoria from the first months. It builds a small woody base that sends up several unbranched leafy stems; from the second or third summer the stem tips carry rose-pink to crimson bracts around hidden green tubular flowers.
growth.source: NARGS 'Adventures with Castillejas' (seed needs winter stratification, alpine species longer; some germinate only in the second spring; hemiparasitic but grows without host); Flora of North America (perennial, 10-40 cm, subalpine-alpine meadows); timings estimated from genus

traits.native_range: Ranunculus adoneus (snow buttercup), Rocky Mountain alpine meadows 3000-4000 m, yellow flowers at snowmelt 5-25 cm
traits.note: leaf/trunk/petiole derived from the plant's shape class; per-species detail where the entry carries it (aroids, cannabis)

growth.juvenile_note: Seeds lie a year in the soil and sprout at the edge of the melting snow: two small oval cotyledons, then a first leaf that is only shallowly lobed; later leaves are cut into narrow, finger-like segments. For several years the plant is a tiny tuft of a few such leaves on a stout root before it bears its glossy yellow flowers right after snowmelt.
growth.source: Wikipedia Ranunculus adoneus (stems 9-25 cm; flowers ~4 cm, 5-10 petals, open within days of snowmelt and last ~10 days; heliotropic; seeds disperse 3-5 weeks after fertilization; 2,500-4,000 m); Galen, Stanton and Scherff snowbed studies (from knowledge); ages estimated

ground.silhouette: woolly grey rosette with star flower

growth.juvenile_note: Seedlings form tiny rosettes of narrow, grey-felted leaves pressed to limestone scree; over one or two short summers they make a small, tight tuft of woolly, silver-white rosettes. Flowering stems then carry the famous star of white-felted bracts around a cluster of small yellowish flower heads.
growth.source: Wikipedia (Leontopodium nivale: flowering stems 3-20 cm, blooms Jul-Sep, 1,800-3,400 m on limestone, full sun, cold stratification improves germination, short-lived perennial in cultivation); timings estimated.

ground.silhouette: flat rosette with huge blue trumpet

growth.juvenile_note: Seed needs winter cold and light; epigeal seedlings are minute, with two round cotyledons and then tiny paired glossy leaves. Grows slowly into a flat evergreen rosette of leathery elliptic leaves; creeping stolons then make a dense mat up to 50 cm wide, and the huge upright deep-blue trumpets usually appear from the 2nd-3rd year.
growth.source: Wikipedia (Gentiana acaulis: to 10 cm, mats to 50 cm wide, evergreen basal rosettes of 2-3.5 cm leaves, 800-3000 m, full sun); alpine seed-raising guidance (cold stratification, slow germination). Ages estimated.

growth.juvenile_note: Seedlings are tiny tufts of bristle-like leaves; the plant spreads mostly clonally into a dense, golf-green-like turf only 1-4 cm tall, underlain by a tough, felty root mat that thickens over centuries. Tiny brownish flower spikes barely rise above the turf in early summer.
growth.source: Estimated from general knowledge of Tibetan Plateau Kobresia pygmaea pastures (dwarf 1-4 cm turf, mainly clonal, maintained by grazing, thick root mats) and alpine sedge growth; no species-specific source could be read.
